clue.text: I study more, initially, after school break

parts.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A pupil vows to work harder once the school holiday arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after school' places the abbreviation first; the initials follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, so a break in that sense.

clue.text: Marry one's husband after son reveals nationality

indicators.note: after says the piece it governs comes second, so the son goes before the marriage

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for son
to marry is to wed
one is I, and the 's adds S
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wedding announcement that somehow discloses where the couple come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after son' moves the son's letter to the front of the build.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedish describes the citizenship or national identity of someone from Sweden, an adjective of nationality.

clue.text: Porthole with a gap is welcome

parts.note: the Port part: Hull is an English port city on the Humber
the hole part: a gap or hole looks like the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone finds a gap where a porthole should be and treats it as a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Porthole into Port and hole and convert each: the port city, then the round letter for a hole or gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hullo is a variant spelling of hello, a greeting used to welcome someone.

clue.text: Drink more rum, boss

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the preceding word is put in a strange order

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss at the bar orders another rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being ordered; it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, an informal word for a boss.

clue.text: Bear market displays reserve

indicators.note: the phrase displays the answer within its own letters, spanning the word break

parts.note: letters running from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: A falling stock market prompts investors to keep funds in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside for a purpose, the same as reserving them.

clue.text: Clear end of day, without question, revealing quickness of thought

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter standing for question is taken away

parts.note: to clear someone of a charge is to acquit them
Q is the abbreviation for question, removed here

indicators.note: end of picks only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A defendant cleared at the close of the day without cross-examination shows a sharp mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Q out of ACQUIT, then add the final letter of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is sharpness or keenness, especially of mind or senses, matching quickness of thought.

clue.text: I will notice them returning about decoration

indicators.note: returning means going back the way they came, so the words before are read from the end

parts.note: the contraction I'll
an ad is a notice in a paper
informal 'em for them
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone promises to spot certain people coming back regarding some ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three pieces turn round; the word for about is then added to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal or round ornamental disc worn as an adornment, a decoration.

clue.text: Run to get a hint in mad scramble

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
a trace is a slight hint of something

explanation.surface: Racing off to pick up a clue during a frantic treasure hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' tempts as RACE, but here it is just the single letter from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the frantic competitive struggle of modern working life, a mad scramble for success.

clue.text: Irrational clue found in abyss

parts.note: surface reading: a clue that makes no sense
setter's reading: a clue with no ground or base beneath it is unfathomable, like a hole without end, which names the abyss

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles about an illogical clue lost in the depths.
explanation.walkthrough: An irrational clue is groundless and unfathomable, words that also describe a hole without end; the answer is that hole, defined by abyss.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit is a chasm so deep it seems to have no floor, which is an abyss.

clue.text: Male cooks dinner for one

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of the word are prepared in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man living alone prepares supper for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' means dinner is one example, not a single diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is one kind of meal, an example of the general term for an occasion of eating.

clue.text: Virtue having reserve of money for head of business's remarkable insight

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: probity is honesty, a virtue
a fund is money set aside

indicators.note: head of picks only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of business, the one replaced

explanation.surface: Praise for a company chief's honesty and the financial reserves behind a brilliant idea.
explanation.walkthrough: In PROBITY, swap the B for FUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity is depth of thought or understanding, so a remarkable insight is an instance of it.

clue.text: Twice one's charged one penny to stop unemployment benefit

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
I is the Roman numeral for one, and P the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Someone on benefits complains of being billed twice, a penny each time.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is Britain's informal name for unemployment benefit. The definition is cryptic: a dipole carries two opposite charges, so it is 'twice charged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipole is a pair of equal and opposite electric charges or poles separated by a small distance.

clue.text: Fighting with no rules, shot untrained revolutionary by a lake

parts.note: a tot is a shot of spirits
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word before is read backwards

parts.note: a raw recruit is untrained

explanation.surface: A green rebel fires a gun beside a lake, ignoring every convention of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed piece comes last in the answer though it comes second in the clue; 'by' puts it beside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Total war is conflict waged without limits on targets or methods, ignoring the usual conventions of warfare.

clue.text: Motors around after tea in conference venues?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about and scattered into another order

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Cars driven about after a tea break at a conference centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that these conferences are online conversations rather than meetings in halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat rooms are online spaces where many people converse together, a playful kind of conference venue.

clue.text: Foreign delivery ignoring old and established practice

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letters for old are dropped

parts.note: handing a suspect over to a foreign country
ex means former or old

explanation.surface: A long-standing custom of sending fugitives abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove EX from the front of EXTRADITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down over time, an established way of doing things.

clue.text: Terrible funeral song not good

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for good is taken out

parts.note: a dirge is a lament for the dead
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A critic pans the music played at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or extremely bad, a direct synonym of terrible.

clue.text: Attractive woman briefly claims the heart of William Tell

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the outer word holds the selected letter
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a babe is slang for an attractive woman, shortened here

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of this seven-letter name

explanation.surface: A woman seeks to win over the Swiss archer of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'William Tell' reads as the folk hero, but Tell is the definition, split away from William.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab is to tell secrets indiscreetly, a verb matching tell in the sense of revealing.

clue.text: Bobby walked round this reportedly to arrest Bohemian

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, who walks his patrol route

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is given by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to arrest

explanation.surface: A policeman patrols around a place to detain a free-living artist.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer, and his regular patrol route is his beat; nick is British slang for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatnik was a member of the 1950s Beat Generation, an unconventional, artistic Bohemian type.

clue.text: Member of clergy nearly late to get ice-cream with sprinkles on vacation

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the late means the dead, cut short here
an ice-cream cone

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of sprinkles

explanation.surface: A cleric, almost running late, buys an ice cream with sprinkles while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptied: remove the inside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaconess is a woman holding the office of deacon in some churches, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Boy working next to church making pale green porcelain

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lad is a boy
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A lad with a job near a church crafts fine pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to church' puts the church's letters ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a Chinese stoneware or porcelain with a distinctive pale grey-green glaze.

clue.text: Small fall?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tumble is a fall

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while its two words also build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble is a trip or lurch that nearly ends in a fall, a minor version of one.

clue.text: Banker welcoming European's guide to life?

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the Gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A banker greets a continental visitor and offers advice on living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money, but the Gnomes of Zurich are Swiss financiers. The question mark marks the definition as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A genome is the full set of an organism's genetic instructions, effectively the blueprint for building life.

clue.text: Mechanism for measuring crimes blocked by police, essentially

indicators.note: blocked by means obstructed from within, so the selected letters sit inside the word for crimes

parts.note: a caper is a crime, especially a heist

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the core of the word, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of police

explanation.surface: A device that gauges how far the police have curbed crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Calipers are an instrument with two hinged legs used for measuring thickness or diameter.

clue.text: Class length

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a level of quality
second meaning: an old unit of distance of about three miles

explanation.definitionFit: League means a grade or standard of ability, and also an obsolete measure of distance of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Calm a boring colleague

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the single letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: an ally is a partner or colleague
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soothe a co-worker who drones on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, describing the colleague; it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To allay fears is to calm or quieten them, a verb meaning to soothe.

clue.text: Bunting is boring, I'd repeatedly snarled

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the contraction written twice

explanation.surface: Someone growls that decorative flags are dull, saying it again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests flags, but here it is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigo bunting is a North American songbird; indigo bird is another name for it.

clue.text: Rounded projection in theatre initially absent

indicators.note: initially absent says the opening letter is missing, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the Globe is Shakespeare's theatre in London

explanation.surface: Something sticks out in a theatre where the opening is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is the London playhouse associated with Shakespeare; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded part that projects or hangs, such as an earlobe or a lobe of a leaf.

clue.text: Broker interrupts Musk interrogation

indicators.note: the answer breaks into the run of the words that follow, sitting across their boundary

parts.note: the end of the name runs into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A financial broker barges into the questioning of Elon Musk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broker' reads as a dealer, but it is 'more broke': skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinter is the comparative of skint, British slang for penniless, so it means more broke.

clue.text: Last couple to sharpen axes with me — a catalyst for change

indicators.note: last couple means the final pair of letters of the next word

parts.note: final two letters
z and y are axes on a graph
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to whet the hatchets with me, a spur to action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' suggests hatchets, but it is the mathematical axes, here z and y.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a biological catalyst, a protein that speeds up chemical reactions in living things.
